question_type: Maximum, over three calendar year-ends, of a currency share (Canadian-dollar liabilities / total liabilities to foreigners), as a rounded decimal

opus_divergence.what_opus_did: The Opus solver got it right (opus_solver_structured = 1). It chose the bank-reported table CM-I-1 'Total Liabilities by Type and Holder' and divided the 'Canadian dollars' row (under 'Major currencies') by the 'Total liabilities to all foreigners' row. It used the 'Calendar Year' column from the latest issue carrying each year (2011_09, 2012_09, 2013_09) and noted that the maximum is the same under every vintage. The adversarial reviewer then found CM-III-1, liabilities reported by NONBANKING business enterprises, which prints calendar-year columns 2009, 2010 and 2011 side by side. The reviewer judged that table 'slightly more likely (~55-60%)' because one table matches the asked range, while CM-I-1 needs three issues. It returned its own answer with verdict 'uncertain', and that answer became final.txt.
opus_divergence.what_right_glm_did: The prompt arm went straight to CM-I-1 and applied the latest-vintage rule: the 'Canadian dollars' row over 'Total liabilities to all foreigners', 'Calendar Year' column, from 2011_09, 2012_09 and 2013_09. These are the same cells as the Opus solver's.
opus_divergence.evidence: Opus worklog.md:25-32 (CM-I-1 identified), worklog.md:67-72 (latest vintage; maximum year stable under every vintage), solution.json:4 (confidence high), solution.json:13-16 (table/denominator/vintage decisions); review.md:14-32 and review.json (verdict 'uncertain'; switches to CM-III-1 on the single-table / range-match argument); prompt [14] (names CM-I-1 and the December vs Mar/Jun/Sep reprint pattern from its lesson), [24]-[28] (latest printing per year, ratio, max)

opus_confidence: high (solver, solution.json:4). The final answer came from the reviewer, who put its own alternative at only ~55-60%.
reviewer_flag: Verdict 'uncertain'. The reviewer confirmed every solver cell and the arithmetic. It then overrode the table choice to CM-III-1 (nonbanking business enterprises), arguing that 'a single-page source is the typical OfficeQA construction' and that CM-I-1 requires stitching three issues (review.md:27-32). The override was wrong.
right_by_principled_choice_or_luck: Principled, through a learned prior rather than by weighing the two tables. The prompt context carried L-cmi1-annual-vintage: CM-I-1 is the bank-reported 'total liabilities to all foreigners' table; December bulletins print CY(year-1) and Mar/Jun/Sep re-print it revised; use the latest bulletin carrying the year. The arm applied it almost word for word at [14]. It never examined CM-III-1: its grep at [11] printed a 'Canadian dollars' row at 2013_12 line 3565, inside the CM-III-1 table that starts at 2013_12:3549 per the Opus reviewer, but it did not open that table. So it never faced the dilemma the reviewer faced.
wrong_glm_arms_same_as_opus: cards: yes, it reached the same final table as Opus's reviewer (CM-III-1, nonbanking enterprises), but for a different reason. It went looking for a Canadian-dollar row in CM-I-1 and read the wrong region, the CM-I-3 by-country rows, at [37]-[38]. It concluded CM-I-1 has only a 'Canada' country row and no currency rows, then settled on CM-III-1 at [39] because that table 'explicitly' has a 'Canadian dollars' row. It never saw CM-I-1's 'Major currencies' rows. none: no. It built the ratio from the Foreign Currency Positions (FCP) tables for major market participants, with an IFS-2 total as the denominator ([33], [41], [50]), a different table family from both of Opus's candidates.
lesson_for_harness: (1) The heuristic 'the asked year range matches one printed table, so that table is intended' is unreliable and keeps recurring; it is the same failure family as Q20. Here it pulled the reviewer to a nonbank table, while the question's wording ('total liabilities to foreign countries by the U.S.') fits the headline bank-reported series (CM-I-1 'Total liabilities to all foreigners'). Semantic fit of row labels and section (banks vs nonbanking enterprises) should outrank a coincidence of year span. (2) Reconciliation must not let a reviewer flip a high-confidence solver answer on a near coin-flip (~55-60%). Keep the solver's answer unless the reviewer finds a concrete error (wrong cell, arithmetic, a violated qualifier), and surface genuine ambiguity instead of switching. (3) A persistent table-location prior (STATE), here the prompt arm's L-cmi1-annual-vintage lesson, let a weak actor get this right cheaply.
notes: The two candidate tables give answers roughly an order of magnitude apart, so this is purely a question of which table is meant. The Opus solver's answer was the same under every vintage of CM-I-1. The cards miss is a navigation/extraction failure (it looked at the wrong part of the capital-movements section) rather than a considered table choice. A 'list every table with a row labelled X' TOOL would have shown it the CM-I-1 and CM-III-1 'Canadian dollars' rows side by side with their section headers.
